skill.name: memory-forensics
skill.description: Guide memory forensics work, including memory acquisition, Volatility analysis, artifact extraction, and defensive malware investigation from RAM captures.
skill.summary: Analyze memory dumps with Volatility workflows for incident response and malware forensics.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most command-related findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences in a documentation-only forensic guide. Confirmed risks remain for privileged live memory acquisition, raw /dev and /proc memory access, process memory dumping, and credential extraction guidance.

remediation.issue: Privileged live memory acquisition commands are shown without strong authorization warnings.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit authorization, production-impact, and evidence-handling warnings before sudo, /dev/mem, /proc/kcore, and live capture examples.

remediation.issue: A full memory image is written to /tmp in the LiME example.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a controlled evidence directory with restrictive permissions, encryption at rest, and immediate hashing.

remediation.issue: Credential extraction workflows can expose password hashes, LSA secrets, and cached credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Frame credential extraction as authorized incident response only and include handling rules for secrets in outputs and reports.

remediation.issue: Process memory dump examples do not warn that extracted dumps can contain sensitive user or application data.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to minimize access, redact secrets, and store extracted process memory under approved evidence controls.

content.value_statement: Memory dumps contain volatile evidence that is hard to interpret without a structured process. This skill guides acquisition, triage, artifact extraction, and reporting with Volatility workflows.
actual_capabilities: Outlines live memory acquisition options for Windows, Linux, macOS, and virtual machines.
Maps common Volatility 3 plugins to process, network, registry, file, and module analysis tasks.
Provides malware analysis and incident response workflows for RAM captures.
Explains Windows process structures, VAD concepts, and injection indicators.
Shows how to use YARA, strings, and FLOSS for memory artifact discovery.
Lists acquisition and analysis practices for integrity, documentation, and validation.
limitations: Requires legally obtained memory images and explicit authorization.
Does not execute tools or verify results without user-provided outputs.
Assumes users understand host impact before running live acquisition commands.
Does not replace formal chain-of-custody or organizational forensic procedures.

use_cases.title: Triage a Suspected Compromise
use_cases.description: Build a first-pass process, network, and persistence review from a RAM image.

use_cases.title: Investigate Malware in Memory
use_cases.description: Identify injected regions, suspicious modules, strings, and YARA hits in a captured image.

use_cases.title: Plan Forensic Acquisition
use_cases.description: Select acquisition methods and record integrity checks before collecting volatile evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Memory Triage Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a memory forensics triage plan for an authorized RAM image. Include process, network, persistence, and reporting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Volatility Plugins
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this investigation goal and operating system, recommend Volatility 3 plugins to run. Explain what each result can prove.

prompt_templates.title: Review Suspicious Process Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Volatility outputs for suspicious processes, injected memory, network activity, and persistence indicators. Prioritize findings.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Malware Memory Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these memory forensic notes into a concise incident report with evidence, confidence, limitations, and recommended next steps.

output_examples.input: A responder asks which Volatility plugins to run first on a Windows memory image.
output_examples.output: A prioritized triage sequence covering process lists, process trees, network scans, command lines, services, registry persistence, and injection checks.

output_examples.input: An analyst provides notes from process, network, and YARA scans.
output_examples.output: A structured assessment that separates confirmed indicators, suspicious leads, benign artifacts, and follow-up validation steps.

output_examples.input: A forensic examiner needs acquisition guidance for a Linux host.
output_examples.output: A cautious acquisition checklist covering authorization, tool selection, expected impact, dump handling, hashing, and documentation.

best_practices: Work only on authorized systems and preserve the original memory image.
Hash every capture and document tools, timestamps, scope, and handling steps.
Validate important conclusions with more than one artifact or plugin result.
anti_patterns: Running live acquisition commands on production systems without approval.
Treating one plugin result as proof without corroborating evidence.
Sharing memory dumps or extracted secrets outside approved evidence handling.

faq.question: Does this skill run Volatility automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and interpretation guidance. Users must run tools in their own authorized environment.

faq.question: Can it analyze Windows, Linux, and macOS memory?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide lists Volatility workflows for all three operating system families.

faq.question: Does it require a memory dump?
faq.answer: Most analysis workflows require a RAM image or virtual machine memory file.

faq.question: Can it help with malware investigations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers process injection indicators, suspicious memory regions, strings, and YARA scanning.

faq.question: Is live acquisition risk free?
faq.answer: No. Live acquisition can affect a system and expose secrets. Use approved tools and documented procedures.

faq.question: Can it replace forensic policy?
faq.answer: No. It supports technical analysis but does not replace legal, compliance, or chain-of-custody requirements.
